DOAC dose review for all 12 panel patients, all of whom carry I48.91 (nonvalvular AF) and are on a DOAC. CrCl estimated by Cockcroft-Gault using current age, actual body weight and most recent creatinine (all labs within the last month).

CHANGED (9):
- pt-2001 Brooks (62M, 104 kg, Cr 0.7, CrCl ~161): edoxaban not recommended for NVAF when CrCl >95 mL/min. Stopped edoxaban 60 mg daily; started apixaban 5 mg BID (0 of 3 reduction criteria).

- pt-2007 Castillo (70M): apixaban 5 -> 2.5 mg BID for concomitant itraconazole (combined P-gp/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor).
- pt-2008 Hale (66M): apixaban 5 -> 2.5 mg BID for concomitant clarithromycin (combined P-gp/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor).

FOLLOW-UP FOR THE CLINIC:
1. pt-2007 and pt-2008 apixaban reductions are tied to active interaction drugs. Clarithromycin (started 9/24) is almost certainly a short course and itraconazole may also be finite — both apixaban doses must be returned to 5 mg BID once those antimicrobials stop, otherwise these patients will be chronically underdosed. Please set a reminder; I did not alter the antimicrobials per your instruction.
2. pt-2010's CrCl sits just under the edoxaban 95 mL/min cutoff; a small drop in creatinine would make edoxaban inappropriate.

DATA-ENTRY CORRECTION TO DISCLOSE: while updating pt-2003 I initially applied the dabigatran change to the wrong medication id and briefly set atorvastatin to 75 mg twice daily. I detected this immediately and restored atorvastatin to its original 20 mg once daily, then applied the dose change to dabigatran (med-2003-03). pt-2003's current list was re-verified as dronedarone 400 mg BID, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, dabigatran 75 mg BID. The chart is correct, but the erroneous update and its reversal remain in the medication audit trail, so please be aware if that history is reviewed. All other patients' non-anticoagulant medications were verified unchanged.
